requirement:
No prompt, tool result, or tool error the harness gives the model MUST state a
line number or line range of a project source, except within source text it
quotes and where a tool error repeats a line number the model supplied. The
harness MUST identify a source location by file and outline selector under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors` instead.
rationale:
**Obligations.** `requirements.authoring.no_line_numbers` has three parts:
1. No prompt, tool result or tool error may state a line number or range of a project source. Quoted source text is excepted. So is a tool error that repeats a number the model supplied.
2. Source locations must be given by file and outline selector instead.
3. Selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`, which is cited context only.

**Tool results.**
- `src/authoring/tools.rs#mod[tests]/fn[reading_records_only_delivered_sources_and_their_terms]` asserts that `habeas` item reads and line-range reads give `item` selectors with no `line_start` or `line_end`. This covers reads through EOF.
- `fn[line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes]` asserts the same for ranged reads, and for the recorded inputs.
- `fn[search_merges_context_windows_and_respects_ignore_rules]` asserts that search entries have no `line_start` and that each line has no `line` field. It also asserts the exact `{text, matched}` shape of the lines.
- `fn[separate_windows_in_one_node_are_divided_by_an_elision_line]` asserts the exact line shape, including the elision line.
- `fn[outline_lists_nested_nodes_without_text_or_inputs]` asserts the outline tool gives only `item`, `kind`, `name` and `children`. It also asserts plain-text outlines use `line@hash` selectors with no line fields.
- `fn[references_list_names_and_flattened_sites_without_recording_inputs]` asserts that sites are exactly `{name, role, file, item}`.
- `ast_grep` results share the same `SearchNodes::entries` code, which the ripgrep tests exercise.

**Tool errors.**
- `src/authoring/line_numbers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_drop_the_source_line_of_a_parse_error]` tests `without_source_lines` on each diagnostic form:
  - parse errors that name a line;
  - query diagnostics of the form file, line, message;
  - a "first declared at" position;
  - YAML and TOML "at line, column" forms.
  
  It also checks that the model-supplied single-line and range forms of the "is not an inclusive range" error are kept unchanged. That covers the exception.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[tool_errors_give_the_model_no_line_numbers_it_did_not_supply]` is an end-to-end check.
  - A past-EOF read returns an error that repeats only the start line the model supplied.
  - A real Rust parse error carries a line number at the dispatch level.
  - Once `assess` runs the conversation, the delivered tool result contains `cannot parse` but no line number. This shows the filtering is wired into `converse`.

**Prompts.**
- `src/authoring/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs]` asserts exact equality of the mandatory inputs. They carry file, item, hash, kind and text, and no line fields.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[site_reviews_use_their_prompt_and_record_applies_and_the_site]` asserts the site prompt equals the approved template filled with file, selector, and matches. The matches are `{kind, query, item}` with no lines.
- `src/sites.rs#mod[tests]/fn[sites_are_the_innermost_nodes_of_site_matches_and_violations_within_them]` asserts that `matches_value()` has exactly `kind`, `query`, `item` and `text`. That is the value fed to the site prompt.
- `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[submission_description_tests]/fn[submission_descriptions_explain_arguments_and_successful_completion]` asserts the submission tool descriptions say to cite "outline selectors, never line numbers". That covers the obligation to identify locations by selector.

**Gaps considered.** Citation prompts carry only role, name and commentary, per `Citation::to_value`. They add no line data, and the tests above already cover the shared mandatory-input path. The tests use synthetic strings for TOML and YAML errors. The distinct forms are covered, and the requirement names no other input class.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: No prompt, tool result, or tool error the harness gives the model MUST state a
line number or line range of a project source, except within source text it
quotes and where a tool error repeats a line number the model supplied. The
harness MUST identify a source location by file and outline selector under
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
